whatItFakes: The state-chamber party-loyalty weight (weights.statePartyLoyalty, 1) is checked against the federal party-unity figure (about 0.90, CQ Vote Studies) because the state roll-call calibration input is not in the repository.
why: The owner ruled on Oct 15 that his own state roll-call input may calibrate this one parameter, with nothing from it shipped or cited; a builder session does not hold that input.
replacement: Run the owner's state roll-call input against the simulated chambers (src/core2/party-loyalty.test.ts measures them), set statePartyLoyalty and the test's target from it, and close this row.

whatItFakes: A state's grocery exemption spares groceries from every level's sales tax in the town, as if every state's local sales taxes followed the state's base. A county's or city's exemption spares only its own tax.
why: No place data says which states let local sales taxes still reach groceries the state exempts (for example home-rule cities, or local option taxes kept on food), so the engine takes the common case of a uniform base.
replacement: A per-state field in the starting-law research (data/research/laws/local-starting-law/sales-tax.json) saying whether local sales taxes follow the state's grocery exemption, sourced from each state's revenue department, read here so a state exemption spares only the levels its base covers.

whatItFakes: A lobbying ban with no numeric period on its law row retains the existing estimated two-year cooling-off period. Researched numeric periods are read from the actual law instead.
why: Some researched yes answers have no structured period, and a newly enacted yes/no bill can omit a duration. This item fixes continuous service and reads available provisions without inventing missing statutory detail.
replacement: Supply the missing structured periods through researched starting-law and voted bill provisions; remove the fallback when every applicable ban carries one.

whatItFakes: A bordering state's law on a question, which weighs on a state legislator's reason to carry the same change (neighborLawWeight), is that state's researched starting law, not its law in force: only the town's state legislates in a played world, so no other state's own acts are recorded and a neighbor never changes its law.
why: Other states keep only coarse results; their legislatures do not sit in the played world.
replacement: Read each bordering state's law in force from the laws a coarse state legislature enacts for it, so a neighbor's change reaches its neighbors the next session.

whatItFakes: Five federal questions (the debt limit, student loan forgiveness, D.C. statehood, federal mandatory minimums, the members' stock trading ban) start as law in force ('no', each cited) and Congress can enact or repeal them from the bill paper, but no engine reads the law, so enacting one moves no money, person or place. The immigration question is read now (counted-moves.ts raises the yearly arrivals from abroad by the researched extra admissions); its labor effect through the outcome web is still unread. National data privacy is read now: the business engine charges employing businesses a compliance cost while it stands (federal-data-privacy-law.test.ts). The disaster cost share is read now (disasters.ts).
why: Each needs a mechanic or a researched size that does not exist yet (a debt ceiling that binds borrowing, an immigration flow, a loan balance record, a disaster cost split, a privacy rule that businesses follow, a statehood and representation change, a sentencing record, a members' holdings record).
replacement: One reader per question, each from its research (data/research/campaigns/federal-questions-2026.json names the cheapest reader for each), so enacting the law changes a record another engine reads.

whatItFakes: How big a gap between a member's wanted budget line and the line in force must be before they file a mid-year amendment (1 percent of the line, spread 0.5 to 3 percent, budgetAmendmentMinShare) is an estimate; no table of local amendment thresholds was found. Real councils also take up contracts, appointments and rezonings that no record here carries.
why: The research names how often local bodies amend budgets mid-year but not a size below which members do not bother.
replacement: Thresholds from sampled local budget-amendment codes and agendas.

whatItFakes: The federal share of public assistance once Congress has states share disaster costs is the 50 percent FEMA's head said was coming (May 15, 2025, Reuters), spread 25 to 75 percent (disasterFederalShareWhenStatesShare); no enacted bill sets it. The cut applies to the federal public assistance the declaration pays the county and town governments.
why: Only the administration's stated plan names the replacement share; no bill or rule has set it.
replacement: The share from the first enacted or introduced text, with the state's own cost taken up by the state government's budget.
